query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A machine‐learned interatomic potential (MLIP) trained on a carefully chosen set of ab initio calculations that include vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling can reproduce accurate free energies for both solid and liquid states, thereby substantially reducing the computational cost for predicting fusion and high‐temperature thermodynamic properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Elemental, binary, or moderate multicomponent high‐entropy systems near melting, with fully interacting electronic and vibrational degrees of freedom.
generation.intervention: Develop and deploy an MLIP that is calibrated against a limited number of high-fidelity ab initio calculations (using density functional theory with explicit vibrational entropy and electron–vibration coupling corrections) for both solid and liquid phases. Then, use enhanced sampling techniques with this MLIP in place of full ab initio molecular dynamics.
generation.conditions: Tested over a range of temperatures spanning the melting point (with focus on a window ±10–20% around the expected fusion temperature) and compositions varying from pure elements and binaries up to moderate multicomponent alloys where TOR-TILD begins to slow down.
generation.structural_mediator: The MLIP mediates structural energetics by effectively capturing the anharmonic potential energy surface and vibrational properties that contribute to the free energies of both phases.
generation.mechanism: Training on key ab initio data enables the MLIP to learn the complex energy landscape – including the subtle contributions from vibrational entropy and electron–vibration couplings – so that molecular dynamics with this ML potential yields free energy differences comparable to explicit ab initio MD but at a fraction of the computational cost.
generation.predicted_outcome: The MLIP-based workflow will achieve phase free energy evaluations and derived observables (e.g. fusion temperature, latent heat) with accuracy comparable to full ab initio methods (deviations within an acceptable error margin, e.g. <5–10%) while being approximately 10–100 times faster than explicit ab initio MD and more scalable than TOR-TILD in multicomponent systems.
generation.baseline: Results from explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD workflows that require full free-energy evaluations with all relevant entropy contributions.
generation.boundary: The method is expected to work reliably for elemental, binary, and moderately complex high-entropy systems around fusion conditions; outside this regime (e.g. extremely complex compositions or states very far from melting), the reliability might deteriorate.
generation.uncertainty: While the approach is supported by success in reproducing ab initio potential landscapes for simpler systems, its extension to accurately capture electron–vibration coupling in multicomponent high-entropy scenarios remains moderately uncertain until validated against full ab initio results.

falsification_experiment.design: Benchmark the MLIP-based free energy evaluation against explicit ab initio MD on a set of test systems (starting from elemental and binary metals) around their melting points. The experiment should compute the solid and liquid free energies, melting point predictions, and latent heats using both methods.
measurements: Phase free energies for solid and liquid states
Error margins relative to full ab initio MD results
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLIP-based workflow produces phase free energies or derived observables (e.g. melting temperature, latent heat) that deviate by more than approximately 5–10% from the explicit ab initio MD benchmarks across the selected test systems, the hypothesis will be falsified.
